quantizacao.d: Storing (and sometimes computing) numbers with fewer bits: each value becomes an 8- or 4-bit code plus a shared scale, \(\hat x = s\,(q - z)\). It trades a small, measured error for 2 to 4× fewer bytes stored and read.

escala-de-quantizacao.d: Distance between neighboring ticks of the quantization ruler: the factor that converts a code into a real value (\(\hat x = s\cdot q\)). In the symmetric form, \(s = \mathrm{amax}/q_{\max}\); in the recipes' FP8, \(s = \mathrm{amax}/448\).

zero-point.d: Integer code that represents the real zero exactly in asymmetric quantization: \(q = \mathrm{round}(x/s) + z\). Being an integer guarantees that structural zeros (padding, ReLU, masks) don't turn into systematic noise.

quantizacao-simetrica.d: A ruler centered on zero (\(z = 0\)) with \(s = \mathrm{amax}/q_{\max}\). It is simpler for the kernel, which only multiplies by the scale, and it suits LLM weights, which are roughly symmetric. Every FP8 and FP4 scale in the recipes is symmetric.

quantizacao-assimetrica.d: A ruler stretched from the minimum to the maximum: \(s = (\max-\min)/(2^b-1)\) and \(z = \mathrm{round}(-\min/s)\). It uses every code when the data is skewed, at the cost of storing and subtracting the zero-point.

quantizacao-afim.d: An asymmetric ruler whose offset is a floating-point number rather than an integer zero-point: \(\hat x = s\,q + b\). With \(b\) equal to the range minimum, it uses all 16 codes of 4 bits, but the real zero no longer lands exactly on a tick. It is the q4 of the dense weights in the TensorFold version of GLM (BF16 scale and bias every 64 weights).

rtn.d: Quantizing each value on its own, rounding to the nearest tick. It minimizes the weight error but ignores how the layer's inputs combine the weights. It is the baseline that GPTQ and AWQ improve on.

clipping.d: Values outside the ruler \([-c, c]\) are pinned to the limit. Shrinking \(c\) sharpens the tick for the common values and flattens the extremes. The optimal limit, which minimizes the MSE, usually sits below amax when there are few bits.

mse.d: Mean squared error \(\frac1n\sum(\hat x_i - x_i)^2\). For uniform rounding with tick \(s\), it is about \(s^2/12\).

sqnr.d: Signal-to-quantization-noise ratio, in dB: \(10\log_{10}(\overline{x^2}/\mathrm{MSE})\). Each extra bit halves the tick and yields ≈ 6.02 dB. A rel RMSE of 2.6% is equivalent to ≈ 31.6 dB.

rel-rmse.d: \(\lVert \hat x - x\rVert_2/\lVert x\rVert_2 = 10^{-\mathrm{SQNR}/20}\): the fraction of the signal that turned into noise. Qwen's FP8-dense measured 0.024–0.027 on the 591 converted tensors, and the verifier fails above 0.06.

outlier.d: A value (or an entire channel) with a magnitude 10 to 100× larger than the rest, common in weights and above all in LLM activations. With a shared scale, it stretches the ruler and its neighbors lose resolution. The defenses are fine granularity, rotations (Hadamard) and keeping the layer in high precision.

granularidade-de-escala.d: How many values share the same scale: per tensor, per channel (output row of the weight), per token (row of the activation), per group or 1D block (16, 32, 64, 128) or per 2D block (128×128). Finer granularity isolates outliers and costs more scale bytes.

escala-por-canal.d: One scale per output channel of the weight (K values per scale). It is GLM's dense FP8 (BF16 scale) and Qwen's FP8-dense (F32 [out]). In column-parallel tensor parallelism it is cut along with the weight's rows; in row-parallel (cut along K) it is replicated on every rank.

escala-por-token.d: One scale per row of the activation \(X\) (one token), usually computed at runtime from the amax of that row. With a per-channel scale on the weight, both come out of the GEMM sum and enter only in the epilogue.

quantizacao-por-grupo.d: One scale every \(g\) contiguous values along K: 16 in NVFP4, 32 in MXFP4 and MXFP8, 64 in DeepSeek's KV. With a small \(g\) an outlier's error stays within its group, and the cost is \(b_s/g\) bits per value.

bits-efetivos.d: Real cost per weight counting scales and zero-points: \(b + (b_s + b_z)/g\). Examples: NVFP4 4.5; MXFP4 4.25; per-channel FP8 with K = 4096 ≈ 8.004 (BF16 scale); EXL3 K=4 on a 4096 × 2048 matrix ≈ 4.0117.

bytes-por-passo.d: Bytes that a decode step reads from memory per rank: active weights (chosen experts, dense weights, lm_head) plus KV and state. In the bandwidth-bound regime, \(t_{\text{step}} \approx B/\text{BW}\). Qwen reads ≈ 9.2 GiB per GPU with batch 1 and MTP=3, and DeepSeek ≈ 16.5–17 GB per rank.

dequantizacao.d: The way back: \(\hat x = s\,(q - z)\), code times scale. In weight-only kernels it happens “on the fly”, in registers, right before the multiplication, and the BF16 matrix is never written to memory.

weight-only.d: Quantizing only the weights (W4A16, W8A16). The kernel dequantizes in registers and multiplies in 16 bits, so the activation suffers no error. It gains bandwidth (decode), not FLOPs.

w4a16.d: Weights in 4 bits, activations in 16. The kernel unpacks and dequantizes in registers and runs the MMA in BF16/FP16. In the recipes: GLM's EXL3 experts (FP16 MMA) and DeepSeek's MXFP4 experts in b12x.

w8a16.d: Weights in 8 bits, activations in 16: GLM's dense FP8 (GLM53_DENSE_FP8, all in the served default) via Marlin, which dequantizes the weight in registers. It cuts bytes in decode with no activation error.

w8a8.d: Weights and activations in 8 bits in the same GEMM, on an FP8 tensor core (2× the BF16 rate on GB10). It gains FLOPs in prefill and adds the error of the activation QDQ. It is Qwen's FP8-dense (FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN). GLM rejected it for KDA.

w4a8.d: Weights in 4 bits and activations in 8 in the same GEMM: it reads the bytes of a 4-bit weight and uses an FP8 tensor core with block scales (on Blackwell, mma … kind::mxf8f6f4, E2M1 × E4M3). The DeepSeek report proposes it (MXFP4 × MXFP8) to speed up the experts' prefill; in the DeepSeek recipe this is not implemented (Marlin MXFP4 already does W4A8 with VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE=fp8, ch. 46).

w4a4.d: Weights and activations in 4 bits, on an FP4 tensor core. The activation is quantized on the fly (dynamic block scale, plus a global scale). It is the regime of Qwen's NVFP4 experts in FlashInfer CUTLASS SM120.

qdq.d: Passing a tensor through \(\hat x = s\cdot Q(x/s)\) and continuing in high precision, as if it had been stored in the low format. It is the error a W8A8 adds to the activation and the node that QAT inserts into training.

quantizacao-estatica.d: A scale fixed offline (for example, amax or MSE on a calibration set) and written into the checkpoint, like NVFP4's input_scale. It costs nothing at runtime, but an out-of-distribution token can saturate.

quantizacao-dinamica.d: A scale computed at runtime, before each GEMM, from the amax of each token or block (for example, act_quant(x, 128) in DeepSeek). It needs no calibration and doesn't saturate. The cost is one reduction per GEMM.

calibracao.d: Running a small sample of real data (hundreds of sequences) through the model to measure activations and choose scales, or to estimate the proxy Hessian. The NVFP4 scales of Qwen's nvidia checkpoint were MSE-calibrated on cnn_dailymail and Nemotron v2.

hessiano-proxy.d: \(\mathbf H = \mathbb E[x x^\top] \approx X^\top X/n\), the second moments of a layer's inputs. The output error of a quantized row is \((\hat w - w)^\top \mathbf H (\hat w - w)\), and GPTQ, LDLQ and the EXL3 converter minimize this error instead of the weight error.

hessiano-sintetico.d: A made-up \(\mathbf H\) in place of the measured one, used to quantize without calibration data. The exllamav3 converter does this for the DFlash2 drafter (caps["uncalibrated_quantize"], init_H_data). Without data, the method doesn't know which inputs matter.

gptq.d: A PTQ method that quantizes one input column at a time and pushes the error onto the columns not yet quantized, using \(\mathbf H^{-1}\) (the Optimal Brain Surgeon update). It accepts a larger weight error in exchange for a smaller output error.

awq.d: Activation-aware Weight Quantization: it protects the few input channels with large activations by multiplying their weights by \(\alpha_k\) and dividing the activation by the same factor (\(XW\) unchanged before quantization). The \(\alpha\) values are chosen by search on a calibration set.

smoothquant.d: A PTQ technique for W8A8: it divides each input channel of the activation by a factor \(\alpha_k\) and multiplies row \(k\) of the weight by the same factor, \(XW = (X\,\mathrm{diag}(\alpha)^{-1})(\mathrm{diag}(\alpha)\,W)\). This way the activation's atypical channels migrate into the weight, which tolerates quantization better.

canal-atipico.d: An activation index \(k\) that is 10 to 100× larger than the others in almost every token. Since it sits inside every row of \(X\), it stretches the ruler of a per-token scale; and a per-channel activation scale would be stuck inside the GEMM sum. That is why it motivates SmoothQuant, AWQ, Hadamard rotations and weight-only.

ptq.d: Post-Training Quantization: quantizing an already trained model, treating rounding as a perturbation to minimize (RTN, GPTQ, AWQ, EXL3, ModelOpt). Almost everything in the recipes is PTQ.

qat.d: Quantization-Aware Training: the training forward contains QDQ nodes, and the gradient goes through the rounding via the STE, so the model learns to tolerate that format. DeepSeek-V4 trained its NoPE KV (FP8, UE8M0 every 64) and its indexer (FP4) this way.

ste.d: The QAT backward trick: since the round function has zero derivative almost everywhere, one pretends it is the identity (\(\partial \hat x/\partial x \approx 1\) inside the ruler, 0 where there was clipping).

dequantizacao-na-busca.d: For tables looked up by row (embeddings, PLE), dequantizing only the rows fetched in the step instead of the whole table. Qwen's _dequantize_embeddings does emb.to(bf16) * weight_scale (FP8) or E2M1 code × block scale × global scale (NVFP4).

qad.d: Training in which the student is the model with quantize-dequantize nodes in the forward pass (as in QAT) and the target is the output distribution of the high-precision model, the teacher, instead of the text. Example: NVIDIA's NVFP4/MXFP8 checkpoint for Qwen3.8 Flash Next, trained against BF16.
